ROOT_CAUSE: The introduction pattern `I'm` greedily captures non-name phrases like 'talking about' because the regex `\b(?:my name is|I am|I'm|This is|hey its)\s+([A-Za-zà-öø-ÿ]+(?:\s+[A-Za-zà-öø-ÿ]+){1,3})\b` allows any words instead of capitalized names. Simultaneously, several sign-off and hyphen patterns fail to match accented characters like 'Rosa-Maria' and full names preceded by specific punctuation or newlines.
RULE: All NAME capture groups for introductions and third-party references must require capitalized words (`[A-ZÀ-ÖØ-ß][a-zà-öø-ÿ]*`), while properly supporting hyphenated names and lowercase prefixes like `de la`.
NEXT_EDIT: Update the `I'm` and introduction regex patterns to enforce proper capitalization for captured names and fix hyphenated name boundaries.
ACTION: KEEP_GOING
